songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Blazing Alligator‑Caution jam, soaring Dark Star, tight rhythm
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a monster Alligator > Caution stretch, a scorching Dark Star and a masterful Eleven. Jerry’s guitar soars while Phil’s bass duels, and the dual drummers drive an explosive groove throughout.
ai_show_review.review: On August 22, 1968 at the Fillmore West the Dead turned in one of their most ferocious late‑’60s performances. The first set builds from a tight Saint Stephen into a thunderous Eleven, then plunges into the gospel‑blues intensity of Death Don’t Have No Mercy before a brief Turn On Your Lovelight. The second set is where the magic erupts: Dark Star unfurls into an improvisational marathon that weaves through Cryptical Envelopment twice, launches into a wild Other One, and then morphs into New Potato Caboose. The centerpiece is the Alligator > Caution jam – a high‑energy, tightly woven sequence highlighted by Mickey Hart’s explosive drum solo and Bill Kreutzmann “going nuts” on the kit. Pigpen’s organ adds perfect psychedelic color throughout, especially on Death Don’t Have No Mercy. The soundboard capture (stereo second set, mono first) is clean and loud enough to showcase every nuance, making this a must‑listen snapshot of the band at peak improvisational intensity.

best_recording.reason: Full‑show soundboard with clear stereo second set and the only source that captures the Alligator > Caution marathon in high quality.

key_highlights: Alligator > Caution jam – a blistering, tightly woven sequence
The Eleven – aggressive bass‑guitar duel and extended solos
Dark Star – soaring guitar work and deep improvisational flow
Mickey Hart’s crystal‑clear drum solo in Alligator

band_performance.Jerry: Soaring, blazing solos on Dark Star, The Eleven and Alligator; vocals rise from low‑key on Saint Stephen to powerful peaks on Death Don’t Have No Mercy.
band_performance.Phil: Aggressive, funky bass that duels with Jerry on The Eleven and delivers a rare extended solo during New Potato.
band_performance.Mickey: Tight, explosive drum work highlighted by a crystal‑clear solo in the Alligator jam; drives the high‑energy flow of the set.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann “goes nuts” on drums during The Other One and provides relentless propulsion throughout the show.
